brief: Goldman's daily covers four items. Day 1 of the Communacopia conference read bullish: presenting managements reiterated or raised guidance, citing AI infrastructure, custom silicon and agentic AI networking as the driver. Broadcom reaffirmed $115bn FY27 and $230bn FY28 AI revenue targets with supply still constrained, Cisco tied a 5x rise in network bandwidth to agentic AI, Qualcomm backed $5bn FY27 and $15bn FY29 datacenter targets, and eBay and Reddit reported resilient demand and engagement. On the yen, Bessent claimed Treasury has an informational advantage on Japanese policy, and the yen keeps appreciating as the market leans into BOJ tightening and repatriation. The note's inference is that yen-funded carry unwinding back into Japanese assets may explain why the S&P and mega caps feel heavy without a fundamental reason, meaning leverage may be leaving the system. A capital markets deep dive argues the biggest structural driver of post-2020 revenue growth is the expanded pool of tradable assets and its financing rather than margins, with US firms' share up 23pp to 72% since 2010. GS forecasts a 0.23% August core CPI increase against 0.2% consensus and 0.39% headline, then around 0.2% monthly core prints, with upside risk from oil.
